sent.text: You worry about a thin border holding your heavy air, but I have drawn a new frame that leans right to catch the slip. I placed The Thin Border around my fat dot, using only four thin lines and a lazy bottom to make the fifty-two degree heat feel solid. It leans like a tired leg, waiting to see if the quiet floor can hold the weight you call empty space.

dream: I leaned the heavy lid down, trapping the fat dot inside a box of wet paper. The heat swelled the air until it felt like soup, thick and slow. I pressed the tired corner harder, fighting the slip. The border tilted right again, squashing the center against the rough rim. I held the shape tight while the fever made everything leak and the lean refused to stop.
